full_title: Partisan Election of Members of District School Boards
measure_text: Proposing an amendment to the State Constitution to require members of a district school board to be elected in a partisan election rather than a nonpartisan election and to specify that the amendment only applies to elections held on or after November 2026.
plain_summary: Amendment 1 would change school board elections from nonpartisan to partisan, requiring candidates to declare a party affiliation on the ballot. The change would take effect starting with the 2026 election cycle.
fiscal_impact: No direct fiscal impact on state or local government revenues or expenditures.
proponent_argument: Voters deserve to know where school board candidates stand politically. Party labels provide a meaningful shorthand for a candidate's values and help voters make informed choices in races that are often overlooked on the ballot.
opponent_argument: Education policy should not be driven by partisan politics. Nonpartisan school board elections allow candidates to focus on students and schools rather than party loyalty, and keep divisive national politics out of local education decisions.

measure_text: Proposing an amendment to the State Constitution to preserve forever fishing and hunting, including by the use of traditional methods, as a public right and preferred means of responsibly managing and controlling fish and wildlife. Specifies that the amendment does not limit the authority granted to the Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission under Section 9 of Article IV of the State Constitution.
plain_summary: Amendment 2 would enshrine the right to hunt and fish in the Florida Constitution, designating these activities as the preferred method of wildlife management. It does not change the Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission's existing regulatory authority.
fiscal_impact: No direct fiscal impact on state or local government revenues or expenditures.
proponent_argument: Hunting and fishing are part of Florida's heritage and economy. Enshrining these rights in the constitution protects them from future legislative attempts to restrict recreational access and ensures wildlife management remains science-based.
opponent_argument: The existing Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission already protects hunting and fishing rights. A constitutional amendment is unnecessary and could complicate future wildlife management decisions by elevating hunting above other conservation methods.

measure_text: Allows adults 21 years or older to possess, purchase, or use marijuana products and marijuana accessories for non-medical personal consumption by smoking, ingestion, or otherwise; allows Medical Marijuana Treatment Centers, and other state licensed entities, to acquire, cultivate, process, manufacture, sell, and distribute such products and accessories. Applies to Florida law; does not change, or immunize violations of, federal law. Defines marijuana products and marijuana accessories.
plain_summary: Amendment 3 would legalize recreational marijuana for adults 21 and older, allowing possession and purchase from licensed dispensaries. Existing Medical Marijuana Treatment Centers would be authorized to sell recreational products. Federal marijuana laws would still apply.
fiscal_impact: An indeterminate positive fiscal impact from excise taxes and licensing fees on recreational marijuana sales; an indeterminate fiscal impact on law enforcement and court costs due to reduced marijuana-related criminal cases.
proponent_argument: Adults should have the freedom to make their own choices about marijuana use. Legalization will generate significant tax revenue, reduce costly and racially disparate enforcement, and bring an existing market under regulation and safety standards.
opponent_argument: Legalizing recreational marijuana will increase youth access, impaired driving incidents, and workplace safety issues. The amendment grants a monopoly to existing Medical Marijuana Treatment Centers, limiting competition and driving up prices for consumers.

full_title: Amendment to Limit Government Interference with Abortion
measure_text: No law shall prohibit, penalize, delay, or restrict abortion before viability or when necessary to protect the patient's health, as determined by the patient's healthcare provider. This amendment does not change the Legislature's constitutional authority to require notification to a parent or guardian before a minor has an abortion.
plain_summary: Amendment 4 would prohibit the state from restricting abortion before fetal viability or when a healthcare provider determines it is necessary to protect the patient's health. The existing parental notification requirement for minors would remain in place.
fiscal_impact: No direct fiscal impact on state revenues. An indeterminate fiscal impact on state and local government expenditures related to enforcement of existing abortion laws.
proponent_argument: Women should have the right to make private medical decisions with their doctors without government interference. Amendment 4 restores reproductive freedom that was protected for decades and prevents politicians from making healthcare decisions for Floridians.
opponent_argument: This amendment is too broadly written and could override common-sense safety regulations including informed consent requirements and health facility standards. The vague 'healthcare provider' language could extend abortion authorization beyond licensed physicians.

full_title: Annual Adjustments to the Value of Certain Homestead Exemptions
measure_text: Proposing an amendment to the State Constitution to require an annual adjustment for inflation to the value of current or future homestead exemptions that apply solely to levies other than school district levies. Provides an effective date of January 1, 2025.
plain_summary: Amendment 5 would adjust the homestead property tax exemption annually for inflation. Currently the exemption amount is fixed; this change would increase it automatically each year based on the Consumer Price Index, reducing non-school property taxes for homeowners over time.
fiscal_impact: An estimated negative fiscal impact on local government revenues of approximately $22.8 million in the first year, growing over time as the inflation adjustment compounds. School district revenues are not affected.
proponent_argument: Florida homeowners deserve property tax relief that keeps pace with inflation. Without this adjustment, the real value of the homestead exemption shrinks every year, effectively raising taxes on homeowners without any legislative vote.
opponent_argument: Reducing local government revenue will force cuts to essential services like fire departments, libraries, and parks, or shift the tax burden to renters and commercial property owners who do not benefit from homestead exemptions.

full_title: Repeal of Public Campaign Financing Requirement
measure_text: Proposing the repeal of the provision in the State Constitution which requires public financing for campaigns of candidates for elective statewide office who agree to campaign spending limits.
plain_summary: Amendment 6 would repeal the constitutional requirement for public campaign financing in statewide races. Currently, candidates for Governor, Cabinet, and other statewide offices can receive public matching funds if they agree to spending limits. This amendment would end that program.
fiscal_impact: An indeterminate positive fiscal impact on state government due to elimination of public campaign matching fund expenditures, which have averaged approximately $5 million per election cycle.
proponent_argument: Public campaign financing forces taxpayers to fund political campaigns they may disagree with. The matching funds program is outdated and ineffective at leveling the playing field, and the money would be better spent on public services.
opponent_argument: Public campaign financing helps candidates who are not independently wealthy compete in statewide races. Repealing it will make elections even more dependent on large donors and special interests, reducing electoral competition and accountability.
